<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

```python
predict(loaded: LoadedModel, input_ids: object = None, *, params: Mapping[str, np.ndarray] | None = None, seq_len: int | None = None, batch_size: int | None = None, backend: object = None, device: object = None, cache: object = None, pack_weights: bool | None = None, family: str | None = None, **options: object) -> np.ndarray
```

Part of [`evoxc_hf.pipeline`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/)

Also available as `evoxc_hf.predict`.

Run the whole forward and return host logits — the one host-facing shorthand.

A transparent composition of explicit primitives — nothing else happens
here:

```
predict(loaded, ids, seq_len=8) ~=
    exe = build(forward_fn(loaded.config, seq_len=8), loaded.config, ...)
    logits = run(exe, loaded.params, ids)
    logits.to(Device("cpu", 0)).numpy()
```

It answers in `numpy`, so its params must be host-addressable (host arrays
or cpu `Tensor`s) — a non-cpu params tree raises `evoxc.DeviceError`
naming the explicit device-resident recipe (`build` with `device=`,
`place_params`, `place_ids`, `run`), never a silent copy
back to the host. The only move it performs is the one documented
`Tensor.to(Device('cpu', 0))` on the *output* of a device-resident
executable.

## Parameters

- `loaded` · `LoadedModel` — the `~evoxc_hf.load.LoadedModel` from
  `evoxc_hf.load_hf` (config + canonical params, plain data).

- `input_ids` · `object` — `(batch_size, seq_len)` integer ids, or `None` (default)
  for all-zero ids of the static shape. Integral dtypes are cast to
  `int32` (`evoxc.DTypeError` otherwise); an `evoxc.Tensor` is
  forwarded to `run` as-is (see `place_ids`). Shapes are
  static, so ids must match `(batch_size, seq_len)` exactly — build
  another length instead of reshaping.

- `params` · `Mapping[str, np.ndarray] | None` — the params to run (default: `loaded.params`). Host arrays (or
  cpu `Tensor`s) only — for a device-resident run use `build` +
  `place_params` + `run` instead. With
  `pack_weights=True` an already-packed tree
  (`evoxc_hf.pack_params` output) is used as-is; a canonical tree
  is packed once here, on the host, before the run.

- `seq_len` · `int | None` — static sequence length, or `None` for
  `evoxc_hf.resolve_seq_len`'s default
  `min(max_position_embeddings, 32)`.

- `batch_size` · `int | None` — static batch size, or `None` for 1.

- `backend` · `object` — `None` (default matrix — see `resolve_build_options`), a
  backend name, or an evoxc backend instance.

- `device` · `object` — `None` or an `evoxc.core.Device` to build/run on.

- `cache` · `object` — an `evoxc.CompileCache` to memoise the build into, or
  `None` for the process-wide default cache.

- `pack_weights` · `bool | None` — opt-in packed weights (default `False`). Packing happens
  once per call, on the host — nothing is re-concatenated per run
  inside evoxc. For repeated runs pass the packed tree explicitly
  (`params=evoxc_hf.pack_params(plan, loaded.params)`) so it is packed
  once.

- `family` · `str | None` — optional explicit family key; when given it must agree with
  `loaded.config.family`.

- `**options` · `object` — compile options forwarded to `build` (and hence to both
  `lower` and `compile`).

## Returns

- `np.ndarray` — np.ndarray: float32 logits `(batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)` on the host. A device-resident executable's output is transferred with one explicit `Tensor.to(Device('cpu', 0))` — the documented, visible move this host-facing helper performs.

## Raises

- `TypeError` — `loaded` is not a `~evoxc_hf.load.LoadedModel` (use
  `evoxc_hf.load_hf`), or `pack_weights` is not a bool.

- `evoxc.ShapeError` — `input_ids` does not match the static
  `(batch_size, seq_len)` shape of this call.

- `evoxc.DTypeError` — `input_ids` is not integral.

- `evoxc.DeviceError` — `params` carries a leaf on a non-cpu device (this
  helper answers in host logits; see the device-resident recipe in the
  message), a host params tree was given to a non-cpu executable (place
  it with `place_params`), or the output could not be
  transferred.

- `evoxc_hf.HFWeightError` — `params` is a canonical tree where the executable
  takes packed inputs (or the reverse), or the tree does not match the
  config's specs.

- `evoxc.BackendError` — the resolved backend is unavailable or rejects the
  graph.
